note: Implementer attempt 1 followed the plan faithfully and hit a real Node ESM limit; the plan's own Risk table pre-authorised duplicating the logic into the .mjs, and it did so with a clear comment. The OUTCOME was rejected, not the reasoning: the duplication reached six functions, leaving 40 tests exercising originals the weekly job never runs, with any future divergence silent. Root cause fixed instead (allowImportingTsExtensions + one explicit .ts extension), the copies deleted, and the script now imports the real modules -- the code that runs unattended is the code the suite covers. Code review then failed R-SEM on attempt 1 because the project-wide tsconfig flag had no Files-to-Change row and had not reached documentation/; that omission was the orchestrator's, not the implementer's, and was corrected in tech-stack.md plus the plan's table and Notes before attempt 2 approved.
